title: Protobuf shim and semantic mapper for OTLP → Tempo v2 ingest
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We receive traces from heterogeneous clients and legacy collectors that emit slightly different OTLP/Protobuf envelopes and Jaeger/Zipkin variants. Tempo v2 ingest in some regions expects a tighter proto schema and attribute naming conventions. This mismatch causes dropped attributes, oversized envelopes that hit our per-request limits, and inconsistent indexing. We need a light-weight, CPU-efficient compatibility layer that transparently normalizes incoming trace envelopes to the Tempo v2 contract and preserves useful legacy fields as mapped attributes.
motivation: Reduce dropped metadata and ingestion errors, enable safe routing of legacy clients to Tempo without client-side changes, and allow schema evolution without immediate client upgrades. Also improve observability for downstream query consistency and reduce failed writes due to envelope size or invalid fields.
implementation_steps: Design proto shim component (stateless) that can be deployed as an ingress filter in the trace gateway
Define a semantic mapping table: common legacy attributes (user.id, span.kind, http.*) → canonical Tempo v2 attribute keys; add backwards-preservation rules (legacy_* prefix) for unmapped fields
Implement lightweight Protobuf normalization: field de-duplication, timestamp normalization, aggregate small attribute values into compressed JSON blob if size threshold exceeded
Add size-aware envelope compression: threshold-based gzip or lz4 with header flag for Tempo to decompress; fall back to attribute pruning when compressor not negotiated
Integrate backpressure signals from downstream (HTTP 429 / 503) to degrade: increase compression aggressiveness and enable drop-low-priority-attributes mode
Instrument metrics (ingest.normalize.duration, ingest.normalize.dropped_attrs, ingest.compress.ratio, ingest.errors) and structured logs for sampling
Add feature flags to gate: normalization on/off, compression policy, attribute-preservation-mode
Write e2e test harness: synthetic OTLP variants + Jaeger envelopes -> assert Tempo v2 accepted, attribute equivalence, and size limits respected
Create canary rollout in a regional gateway, monitor error/latency dashboards, iterate on mapping rules
Document mapping table and add runbook for mapping updates and rollbacks
acceptance_criteria: Gateway normalizes at least 95% of synthetic legacy envelopes to Tempo v2 without attribute loss (unless explicitly pruned by policy)
End-to-end ingestion failure rate for legacy clients in canary region decreases by 90% compared to baseline
Average added CPU per gateway instance stays below 10% at 95th percentile traffic for canary
Envelope size reduction (before vs after normalization+compression) is >= 40% for large payload cases
All new metrics emitted and visualized in console dashboards with alerting configured for error spikes and compression failures
Feature flags allow immediate disable of normalization and compression, and rollback path exercised in staging
qa_plan: Unit tests for each mapping rule and edge-case attribute types
Integration tests exercising compressed and uncompressed paths against a tempo v2 mock endpoint
Load test with replayed production trace payloads to measure CPU, latency, and compress ratio
Chaos test: simulate downstream 429/503 to verify backpressure adaptation behaves as expected
Manual verification: search traces with canonicalized attributes in Tempo and compare results with raw input mappings
rollout_plan: Deploy to staging gateway behind feature flag and run full e2e harness
Canary rollout: 5% of regional traffic for 48 hours, monitor ingest metrics and query correctness
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks if no regressions
Post-rollout: run a two-week comparison of indexing and query latencies, and confirm cost impact on storage/ingest
If regressions detected: flip feature flag off and execute rollback playbook
